label: text
text: SIR BASIL THOMSON IN DOCK

label: text
text: POLICIMAN'S ALLEGATIONS.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: A huge crowd besieged Marlborough Police Court on the appearance of Sir Basil Thomson to answer two summonses—one accusing him of indecency with a woman in Hyde Park and the other requiring him to show cause why his recognisances of £5 should not be fogseited for non-appearance in Court on the day named in the original summons.

label: paragraph_title
text: Temptation?

label: text
text: A policeman gave evidence that after the arrest accused told him that he was Sir Basil Thomson and if his friends knew about this he would be ruined. Subsequently, the policeman alleged, accused said that if witness overlooked the matter he could leave the police to-morrow. The policeman replied that accused should not tempt him, adding: "You know how impossible it is for me to let you go. The police is my sole means of existence."

label: paragraph_title
text: Recognised At Station

label: text
text: Counsel for the prosecution said that accused at the Police Station, where an Inspector recognised him, asked that his name be entered as Hugh Thomson. He was released on bail of £5 but failed to appear in Court. Subsequently he wrote explaining that he went to Bow Street by mistake. Accused appeared at Marlborough Street on December 16 for service of a summons on a woman who was a young pantomime artist, who was arrested and fined on December 22.

label: text
text: The case was adjourned.

label: text
text: "A Varied Career.

label: text
text: Sir Basil Thomson is the third son of the late Archbishop Thomson, of York, and was born in 1861, Educated at Eton and New College, Oxford, he entered the Colonial Civil Service and went to Fiji and thence to Tonga.

label: vision_footnote
text: Sir Basil Thomson.

label: text
text: During his term of office trouble arose in the Tongan group, and Sir Basil then not 30 years of age found the mantle of Prime Minister cast upon his shoulders.

label: text
text: Some of the exploits of his predecessor in the Premiership, the famous Shirley Baker, he recounted in an interesting book, "The Diversions of a Prime Minister." He was transferred to British New Guinea, where he was awarded the silver medal of the Royal Humane Society for saving life at sea.

label: text
text: In 1893 Sir Basil was given charge of the King of Siam when he was being educated in this country.

label: text
text: In 1896 he was called to the Bar by the Inner Temple; and in the same year began his long connection with crime and criminals by entering the prison service as deputy governor of Liverpool Prison. He held a similar post at Dartmoor, and was subsequently governor successively of Northampton, Cardiff, Dartmoor, and Wormwood Scrubs prisons till 1908, when he became inspector of prisons and secretary to the Prison Commissioners.

label: text
text: In 1900, while at Northampton, he was again sent out to the Pacific by the Colonial Office as Special Commissioner to negotiate treaties with two of the native Governments.

label: text
text: In 1913 Sir Basil was appointed in succession to Sir Melville Macnaghton, Assistant Commissioner of the Metropolitan Police, and in 1910 Director of the special Branch. He retired in 1919. Among his literary works perhaps the most fascinating is his "Story of Dartmoor Prison," and he is also the author of "South Sea Yarns," "A Court Intrigue," "The Indiscretions of Lady Asenath," "Discovery of the Solomon Islands," "Savage Island." UNPRECEDENTED SCENES
IN FRANCE.

label: text
text: FATAL COLLAPSE OF A HOUSE.

label: text
text: (Rouiler's Service.)

label: text
text: The likelihood of continued rain is causing the utmost anxiety. Already the Oise has benten all records, including the floods of 1910 and 1920, having risen twenty feet. The triangle between Creil, Beauvnis, and Noyon is a vast sheet of water.

label: text
text: Training on the main line to Belgium are obliged to slow down for many miles, whilst sometimes the floors of the carriages are swamped.

label: text
text: The villages in the flooded areas are being hurriedly evacuated and household goods are being transported on rafts.

label: text
text: The flooding of "the water works at Compeigne resulted in a limited supply of drinking water and rationing from barrels.

label: text
text: The rise of the Aisne flooded many streets in Soissons. A train between Cien and Saintlo was abandoned after the passengers were rescued.

label: text
text: A child was killed and three persons injured as the result of the collapse of a house at Caen, which caused enormous damage. Some of the estimates amount to twenty million francs.

label: text
text:
TORRENTS IN STREETS
The rise of the Meuse converted the streets in Mezières into rushing torrents.

label: text
text: It is feared that 20,000 workers in the Meuse Valley will be idle for three weeks in consequence of the flooding of the factories.

label: text
text: Amsterdam. Jan. 4.

label: text
text: The water has fallen a yard below yesterday's highest level at Maestricht, so the trains to Giege and the northern parts of Holland are running, but not for public traffic.

label: text
text: Their Majesties this morning viewed the damage at Maestricht, where many of the homeless people are sheltered in the military barracks at Shertogenbosch.

label: text
text: In view of the extent of the disaster it is remarkable that so far there have been no fatalities, although two women went insane as a result of their anxiety and distress.

label: text
text: POSITION IN BELGIUM

label: text
text: Their Majesties to-day paid a very lengthy visit to the inundated regions around Namur and Dinant.

label: text
text: The situation in the Liege, Namur, and Brussels districts has greatly improved, but the position in the low-lying districts, notably in the Waes area, has become worse.

label: text
text: A ROYAL DONATION.

label: text
text: Their Majesties have subscribed two million frames to the national fund for the victims of the floods, comprising the money presented to them on the occasion of their silver wedding last year, besides a personal gift of 100,000 francs.

label: paragraph_title
text: EARLIER NEWS.

label: text
text: Rain is... still falling and the flood-waters are rising. The River Waal, near Wymegen, is at the highest for very many years. Many houses in the Poldesr neighbourhood of Amsterdam are submerged.

label: text
text: The viaduct and railway station at Beugen, north-east of Brabant, collapsed under pressure of the rising water.

label: text
text: Between Flushing and Gogh a train was derailed owing to the sinking of a dyke.

MOTHER.

label: text

label: text
text: Queen-Mother Margherita has passed away.

label: text
text: [A Rome message of December 18, which did not reach Hongkong, stated: — Queen-Mother Margherita, whose condition at Bordighera, owing to congestion of the lungs, has given rise to anxiety, passed a quiet night, though the local symptoms are unchanged and the royal patient's temperature is high.]

label: doc_title
text: TO SAVE GREECE.

label: text
text: DICTATORSHIP ESTABLISHED

label: text
text: (Reufer's Service.)

label: text
text: Athens, Jun. 4.

label: text
text: The Commander of each barracks announced that a Dictatorship had been proclaimed and all must contribute to the task undertaken by the Army for the nation's good. The statement concluded: "On your bayonets only does the establishment of the Dictatorship depend."

label: text
text: FORMAL ANNOUNCEMENT. Athens, Jan. 4.

label: text
text: General Pangalos made his announcement at a banquet given by Officers of the Republic Guard.

label: vision_footnote
text: The New Dictator.

label: text
text: It evoked demonstrations of enthusiasm, which were renewed by the Guard during a parade of the streets in the evening.

label: text
text: General Pangalos said that he was preparing a programme based solely on armed forces.

label: text
text: WHO IS PANGALOS?

label: text
text: General Pangalos has been Premier since June, when he organised a coup d'état in the Army and compelled the resignation of the Michalacopulas Government. He was largely instrumental in the events leading to the deposition of King George II. in 1923, and the establishment of a Republic. He presided at the court-martial in 1922, which ordered the execution of the former Premier, M. Gounaris, and three other ex-Ministers on the charge of responsibility for the overwhelming defeat of the Greeks by the Turks in Asia Minor.

label: text
text: ... There has been much speculation recently regarding the possibility of the return of King George II to the throne.

label: paragraph_title
text: TEA DANCES

label: text
text: CHINESE AMUSEMENT PARK

label: text
text: . FANN.

label: text
text: Lee Garden (formerly Jardine's Hill) at Causeway Bay has been the scene of successful tea dances during the holidays, a large number of Europeans availing themselves of the opportunity to enjoy the floor and, at the same time, enjoy the many sights.

label: text
text: A feature of this park is the minute care with which "sets" copied on exact lines, have been reproduced of romantic places in Chinese history and mythology.

label: text
text: Facing the dance hall is a life-size set of figures representing a faithful minister who spent a long captivity among the wilds of Mongolia with a devoted wife, child and some sheep. The “Goddess of Mercy” stands close by and there are many freak erections to be examined.

label: text
text: The next tea dance will be held to-morrow afternoon.

label: text
text: POLICE JUSTIFICATION

label: text
text: In the course of his conclusions on the Shanghai affair of May 30 into which he enquired as Britain's judicial representative. Sir Henry Cowper Gollan. Chief Justice of Hongkong, remarks as follows:—

label: text
text: After full and careful consideration of all the evidence adduced by the witnesses, of their demeanour, and of the inherent probabilities of the respective stories told by them, I am clearly of opinion that the evidence given by the police witnesses, and supported by the large body of independent testimony, is substantially correct, and that Inspector Everson was justified in coming to the conclusion that, if the crowd had not been fired upon, the lives of the police under his command would have been sacrificed, and the crowd would have gained possession of the Louza Police Station; with results that might have been most serious in view of the quantities of arms and ammunition stored there.

label: text
text: And it is also to be remembered that, a mob had in December 1905 seized and destroyed the Louza Police Station, in the face of strenuous opposition offered by a body of unarmed police.

label: paragraph_title
text: Mob Psychology.

label: text
text: A matter that struck me was the rapid change that, according to the evidence, took place in the state of mind of the crowd, within a period of about 15 minutes, and without the commission of any acts by the police tending to irritate the crowd. At one time, the group of students who had been ejected from the charge room, and the others who had joined them, were being induced to move back by a small body of police. The leading idea in the mind of this crowd would then seem to have been to obtain the release of the students who had been detained.

label: text
text: Then this smaller retreating crowd was stopped by a much larger crowd with elements of an unruly character in it, a student coming from the direction of the Louza Police Station waved to the amalgamated crowd to return in the direction of the Station, the movement to the east was arrested; certain persons developed a high state of excitement which communicated itself to the rest of the crowd, the crowd turned on the police, and finally was worked up to attack the policemen who guarded the approach to the Louza Police Station. The evidence of Major Hilton-Johnson throws light on this aspect of Chinese mob psychology. He particularly referred to first, the inflammability of the Chinese temperament and the rapidity with which, in the mass, they are capable of passing from a state of quiescence to a state of frenzy which soon gets beyond their control; second, the length to which a mob raised to that pitch of fury, will proceed and the excesses it will commit unless the mob spirit subsides or is quelled.

label: text
text: ENQUIRY INVIDENCE.

label: text
text: The second-in-comphand of the pirate, gang, which took possession of the "Fungohow" and carried off the boxes of silver dollars it was carrying, claimed to have been educated at Queen's College, Hong Kong; this transpired in the course of the inquiry at Shanghai into the circumstances of the piracy.

label: text
text: Evidence of his conversation with this man was given by the Chief Officer who, questioned on the matter of gen. and piracy prevention, mensures, said that if a ship carried bullion it would be best not to carry Chinese poeers.

label: text
text: Finding 1 of the Court of Enquiry were I

label: text
text: 'Having carefully reviewed the evidence and the circumstances above stated, the Court sees no ground for blaming the conduct of the ship's officers or crew. In the light of this experience which had been gained by this incident, it considers, however, that greater care should be exercised in future in the matter of Chinese passengers. If possible, some record should be kept of the Chinese passengers to whom tickets are sold and they should be searched for arms before the ship leaves the port. In the case of ships carrying bullion or sp.seie, it might be advisable, at all events as a temporary measure, either to take no Chinese passengers or else to carry into armed guard in addition to the crew.'

label: text
text: "The Court is also of the opinion that the provision of wireless, which it understands is shortly to be installed on the China Navigation Company's ships running between Shanghai and Tientain, would as an additional deterrent to pirates contemplating a seizure of this nature."

label: text
text: "Finally it desires to record its conviction that the only satisfactory way of dealing with the pirate menace is to destroy the pirate bases on shore, without which attacks such as that on the s.s. "Tungchow" would be impossible."

text: ROOF ABLAZE.

label: paragraph_title
text:
FOOTBALL STAND
DAMAGED.

label: text
text: YESTERDAY EVENING'S SCENE

label: text
text: Residents at Happy Valley were treated to a spectacular sight at 6 o'clock yesterday evening when the roof of the spectators' stand on the Hongkong Football Club ground was destroyed by fire about one quarter of its length.

label: text
text: A fire engine arrived fifteen minutes later, and running down a hose from the new hydrant at Wong Nei Chong Road, subdued the flames and saved the remainder of the structure.

label: text
text: Curiously, the fire had its origin in the roof at one end, which obviously points to some lighted material having been thrown on to it.
